chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from

Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Layth ibn Sa'd. He said: I said to Ka'b while he was at Mu'awiya's court: 'How do you find the description of the Prophet's birth (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), and do you find any virtue for his progeny?' Ka'b turned to Mu'awiya to gauge his inclination, but God, Mighty and Exalted, caused speech to flow upon his tongue, and (Mu'awiya) said: 'Speak, O Abu Ishaq — may God have mercy on you — what do you have to say?' Ka'b said: 'I have read seventy-two books, all of which were revealed from heaven, and I have read all the scrolls of Daniel, and I found in all of them mention of his birth and the birth of his progeny, that his name is well known, and that no prophet was ever born upon whom the angels descended except Jesus and Ahmad (blessings of God upon them both).

upon them both. And the veils of Paradise were never drawn for any human woman except Maryam and Aminah, the mother of Ahmad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). And the angels were never charged with guarding a woman who carried a child except Maryam, the mother of the Messiah, and Aminah, the mother of Ahmad. Among the signs of his conception was that on the night Aminah conceived him (may God's blessings be upon him and his family), a caller called out in the seven heavens: 'Rejoice, for tonight Ahmad has been conceived!' And likewise in the earths, and even in the seas. There was no creature that walked on the earth nor any bird that flew that day except that it knew of his birth. And seventy thousand palaces of red ruby and seventy thousand palaces of fresh pearl were built in Paradise on the night of his birth. It was said: 'These are the palaces of the birth.' The gardens of Paradise were adorned and it was said to them: 'Quiver

and adorn yourself, for the Prophet of those devoted to you has been born.' So Paradise laughed that day, and it has been laughing until the Day of Resurrection. I have also heard that a fish from the fish of the sea, called Tamsoosus, the master of all fish, has seven hundred thousand tails, upon whose back there walk seven hundred thousand bulls, each one larger than this world, each bull having seven hundred thousand horns made of green emerald, not knowing of them — it convulsed with joy at his birth. Had God, Blessed and Exalted, not stabilized it, it would have turned the earth upside down. And I have heard that on that day, no mountain remained except that it called out to its neighbor with glad tidings, saying: 'There is no god but God.' And all the mountains submitted to Abu Qubays in honor of Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). And for forty days the trees sanctified God with their varied branches

and their fruits in joy at his birth. And seventy columns of various kinds of lights were erected between heaven and earth, none resembling another. Adam was given glad tidings of his birth, and his beauty was increased seventy-fold; he had been experiencing the bitterness of death and that had touched him, but it was removed from him. And I have heard that the Kawthar stirred and quivered in Paradise and scattered seven hundred thousand palaces of pearl and ruby as a gift of joy at the birth of Muhammad (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). And Iblis was muzzled and shackled and thrown into a fortress for forty days, and his throne was submerged for forty days. And all the idols fell over and cried out and wailed. And they heard a voice from the Ka'ba: 'O family of Quraysh! The bearer of good tidings has come to you, the warner has come to you, with him is the glory of eternity and the greatest profit. He is

the Seal of the Prophets. And we find in the books that his progeny are the best of people after him, and that people will remain in safety from punishment as long as any of his progeny walks upon the face of the earth.' Mu'awiya said: 'O Abu Ishaq, and who are his progeny?' Ka'b said: 'The children of Fatimah.' His face darkened, he bit his lips, and he began playing with his beard. Then Ka'b said: 'And we find the description of the two martyred chicks, and they are the two chicks of Fatimah — the worst of creation shall kill them.' He said: 'And who will kill them?' He said: 'A man from Quraysh.' Then Mu'awiya stood up and said: 'Rise if you wish.' So we rose.

key_terms.الْفَرْخَيْنِ الْمُسْتَشْهَدَيْن: The two martyred sons — referring to Imams Hasan and Husayn
key_terms.خَاتَمُ الْأَنْبِيَاء: Seal of the Prophets — the final prophet in the line of prophethood
key_terms.عِتْرَة: Progeny, the Prophet's close family (the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.مَوْلِد: Birth, specifically the birth narrative of the Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What cosmic signs accompanied the birth of the Prophet Muhammad according to Ka'b al-Ahbar?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a dramatic exchange at the court of Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, where the Jewish scholar Ka'b al-Ahbar, prompted by divine inspiration, narrates wondrous cosmic signs that accompanied the conception and birth of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Drawing from seventy-two heavenly books and the scrolls of Daniel, Ka'b describes celestial celebrations, the submission of creation, and the construction of palaces in Paradise — all confirming the Prophet's supreme status. The narration culminates in Ka'b's identification of the Prophet's progeny as the descendants of Fatima, causing Mu'awiya notable discomfort, and includes a prophetic reference to the martyrdom of the two sons of Fatima (Imams Hasan and Husayn) at the hands of 'a man from Quraysh.' This text belongs to the genre of mawlid (birth narrative) literature and reflects Shia theological emphasis on the Ahl al-Bayt's divinely ordained virtue.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim from

Muhammad b. Sinan from Ziyad b. al-Mundhir from Layth b. Sa`d. He said: I said to Ka`b [al-Ahbar] while he was with Mu`awiya: How do you view the birth (mawlid) of the Prophet (s), and do you find any virtue in his progeny? So, Ka`b turned to Mu`awiya to see his inclination. Then, Allah caused his tongue to speak, and he said: Go ahead, Aba Ishaq, may Allah have mercy on you, what do you have? So, Ka`b said: I have read seventy-two books, all of which have descended from heaven. I have read all the scrolls of Daniel, and in all of them, I found his birth and the birth of his progeny mentioned. His name is known. Surely, the angels did not descend upon the birth of any prophet except `Isa and Ahmad (s).

No barrier from Paradise was put over any human except Maryam and Amina the mother of Ahmad (s). The angels were not entrusted with a pregnant woman other than the mother of the Messiah and Amina the mother of Ahmad. One of the signs of his conception was that, on the day that Amina became pregnant with him (s), a caller called in the seven heavens, the Earths, and the seas: “Be glad, for Ahmad has been conceived on this night.” There did not remain a creature that crawled on the Earth nor a bird that flew except that it knew about his birth. On the night of his birth, seventy thousand palaces of red ruby and seventy thousand palaces of fresh pearl were built in Paradise. It was said: “These are the palaces of the birth”. The Gardens were decorated, and it was said to them: “Shake [off your fruits] and decorate, for a prophet of your friends has been born.”

So, Paradise smiled on that day, and it will remain smiling until the Day of Resurrection. A whale from the whales of the sea called Tamsusa – and he is the master of whales; he has seven hundred thousand tails, and seven hundred thousand bulls riding on his back which he does not feel – each of which is larger than this world, and each of which has seven hundred thousand horns of green emerald – [this whale] was struck with happiness by his birth. Had Allah not caused him to remain steadfast, then he would have turned lopsided. I was told that, on that day, a mountain did not remain except that its owner called out in happiness: “There is no god but Allah.” All the mountains humbled themselves toward [Mount] Abu Qubays to honour Muhammad (s). The trees, with their various branches, sanctified [Allah], and their fruits were gladdened by his birth.

Seventy pillars of light appeared between heaven and Earth, and each of which was distinct from the other. Adam was given glad tidings about his birth, so his goodness increased seventyfold. He had found the bitterness of death, but when this [news] touched him, it brought joy to him. I was informed that al-Kawthar was struck in Paradise, and it shook, and it hurled seven hundred thousand palaces of pearl and ruby as confetti for the birth of Muhammad (s). Iblis was stiffened, shackled, and thrown into imprisonment for forty days. His throne drowned for forty days. All the idols collapsed, shrieked, and wailed. They heard a voice from the Ka`ba: “O Family of Quraysh! A giver of glad tidings has come to you. A warner has come to you. With him is eternal glory and the greatest triumph. He is

the Seal of Prophets.” We find in the books that his progeny is the best of people after him, and that the people will be safe from chastisement as long as [one] from his progeny remains walking in the abode of this world. Mu`awiya said: O Aba Ishaq! Who is his progeny? Ka`b said: The descendants of Fatima. So, his face frowned, he bit his lip, and he began pulling on his beard. So, Ka`b said: We also find the description of two martyred sons, and they are the sons of Fatima. They will be killed by the evillest of creation. He said: Who will kill them? He said: A man from Quraysh. So, Mu`awiya stood and said: Stand if you wish. So, we stood.
